### 📦 Phase 26: Unified Dual-Role Accounts & Explicit Role-Switching
> Resolves the identity collision where `Account.email @unique` blocks an artist from booking as a client under the same email profile.
- [ ] **26.1: Dual-Role Core Engine Setup**
  - **Prerequisite Architecture pass:** Enforce the design constraint that an artist's linked client identity must use a standard `ClientProfile` row so precharge models apply naturally.
  - **Architecture decision (confirmed):** `Account.role` stays the account's permanent home role; a new `Session.activeRole` column holds the per-session effective role (dual-role accounts may hold concurrent sessions in different roles; `activeRole` must stay server-trusted for `src/proxy.ts` gating, so it lives in the DB, not a client-readable cookie). Becoming dual-role is an explicit "Become a client" settings action (never automatic, never auto-switches into the new role afterward). Shared Instagram-handle/18+ validation primitives move to `src/lib/clientProfileValidation.ts`; the `ClientProfile` find-or-link matching logic stays auth-owned (not shared with booking's guest-checkout `resolveGuestClientProfile`, whose overwrite-on-repeat-visit semantics are wrong for a one-time authenticated link).

### 📦 Phase 27: Auth Session Security & Lifecycle Hardening
- **Status:** 27.1–27.2 scoped; 27.3–27.5 and 27.7 remain unscoped (each will get its own layered breakdown pass closer to when it's picked up).
- **Sequencing (confirmed):** Paused pending **28.1** (mocked-Prisma foundation). 27.1.2.1, 27.4.2.2 and 27.5.2.1 already specify "mocked-Prisma unit tests", but no Prisma mock exists anywhere in the repo yet — resume at 27.1 once 28.1 lands.
- **Objectives:** Gaps surfaced during review of the Phase 26 dual-role/session work, ordered by priority for production risk:
  - **27.1: Login throttling/lockout** — `loginArtist`/`loginClient` do scrypt-verify with no rate limit or attempt counter; no backstop against credential stuffing beyond hash cost. Highest priority: active, unmitigated attack surface.
    - **Design (confirmed):** account-scoped lockout (no IP-based tracking — no request-IP capture infra exists in the repo, out of scope here). Two new `Account` fields: `failedLoginAttempts Int @default(0)` and `lockedUntil DateTime?`. A locked account returns the *same* generic `INVALID_CREDENTIALS_ERROR_MESSAGE` (never a distinct "account locked" message) so lockout state doesn't become a new enumeration vector on top of the existing generic-error protection — `verifyPassword` is skipped entirely while locked. A failed attempt after a naturally-expired lockout window restarts the counter at 1 rather than instantly re-locking. Successful login resets both fields. Constants `MAX_FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS = 5` / `LOGIN_LOCKOUT_DURATION_MS = 15 min` land in `src/domains/auth/constants.ts`. Accepted tradeoff: skipping `verifyPassword` while locked is a minor timing side-channel (locked responses return faster than wrong-password ones); not hardened further given the app's risk profile. No UI/Hook/View changes needed — `useArtistLogin`/`useClientLogin` already forward any `result.error` string generically into the existing login forms' error state, and the lockout path reuses the existing message, so the presentation layer is untouched.
    - **Confirmed 6-layer sub-task breakdown** (each leaf = one isolated PR; do not combine):
      - [x] **27.1.1.1** Data Gateway — add `Account.failedLoginAttempts Int @default(0)` + `Account.lockedUntil DateTime?` columns + migration. No app code.
      - [x] **27.1.2.1** Domain Service — `recordFailedLoginAttempt(accountId)` in `services/recordFailedLoginAttempt.ts`. Implemented as a bounded-retry compare-and-swap (`findUnique` then a CAS `updateMany` scoped to the exact row values read) rather than a blind read-then-write, closing a TOCTOU race where two concurrent failed logins could both read count N and both write N+1 (architecture.md §8.A); uses Node's clock throughout to stay consistent with 27.1.2.3's lockout check; wrapped in a never-throw try/catch (accountId-only logging) so a bookkeeping failure can't turn a wrong-password login into an uncaught 500. Mocked-Prisma unit tests: first failure, Nth failure hits `MAX_FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS`, failure after a naturally-expired lockout restarts the counter at 1, CAS-miss retry against fresh state, retries-exhausted (logs, doesn't throw), no-op when already locked by a concurrent request, no-op when the account no longer exists, and an unexpected DB failure is swallowed and logged.
      - [x] **27.1.2.2** Domain Service — `resetFailedLoginAttempts(accountId)` in `services/resetFailedLoginAttempts.ts` (mocked-Prisma unit test).
      - [x] **27.1.2.3** Domain Service — wire the lockout check + `recordFailedLoginAttempt`/`resetFailedLoginAttempts` into `loginArtist.ts` and `loginClient.ts`; extend their existing `.test.ts` files (locked account short-circuits before `verifyPassword`, failed attempt records, success resets).
      - [x] **27.1.3.1** Controller/Action — N/A. `loginAction`/`loginClientAction` already pass `result.error` through unchanged; reserved explicitly per the vertical-slice requirement rather than silently skipped.
      - [x] **27.1.4.1** UI Primitive — N/A. Existing `LoginForm`/`ClientLoginForm` error rendering already covers this.
      - [x] **27.1.5.1** Domain Hook — N/A. `useArtistLogin`/`useClientLogin` already forward `result.error` generically.
      - [x] **27.1.6.1** View & Route — N/A. No new routes or page composition required.
  - **27.2: Defensive error isolation on internal DB paths** — `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount` uses `findUniqueOrThrow` inside a transaction; the calling action (`setUpClientProfileAction`, the actual name in code — the roadmap's `becomeClientAction` label in Phase 26 doesn't match `actions.ts`, worth reconciling when Phase 26 closes) doesn't catch it, so an edge-case failure bubbles as an uncaught 500. Apply the same try/catch isolation discipline architecture.md §6 requires for Stripe calls to this internal DB path.
    - **Design (confirmed):** wrap the entire `prisma.$transaction(...)` call in `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount.ts` in one try/catch (sufficient by Prisma semantics — any throw inside the callback surfaces at the outer call, so no nested try/catch is needed; the transaction's existing `{success:false,...}` business-error returns are untouched). Deeper analysis surfaced two things beyond a bare wrapper: (1) `ClientProfile.instagramHandle`/`email` are both `@unique` with no explicit transaction isolation level set (default Postgres Read Committed), so the check-then-`create` flow has a genuine TOCTOU race — two concurrent submits can both pass the "no match" check and collide on `tx.clientProfile.create` with Prisma error P2002; (2) `useSetUpClientProfile.ts`'s `onSubmit` has no try/catch around `await setUpClientProfileAction(...)`, so an uncaught throw today leaves the form in a stuck-spinner state, not just a generic 500 — the concrete reason this must be fixed at the service boundary rather than left to the hook. Unlike the sibling precedent in `booking/services/updateClientProfile.ts` (which maps its own P2002 to one unambiguous message and rethrows everything else), this service must never rethrow (that's exactly the stuck-spinner bug) and must not map P2002 to a specific "already linked" message (ambiguous here — could mean self double-submit *or* a genuine two-user race, and guessing wrong is actively misleading). Both the P2002 case and any other unexpected error return the same new generic, retry-oriented `SET_UP_CLIENT_PROFILE_UNEXPECTED_ERROR_MESSAGE`; a retry self-corrects via the service's existing lookup logic either way. P2002 is still distinguished from other errors in the `console.error` log line only (accountId, never PII), for ops triage. `findUniqueOrThrow`'s P2025 is structurally near-unreachable (`Session.account` has `onDelete: Cascade`, so a live session can't reference a deleted account) but still caught defensively — no session-invalidation logic is built around it, since no reachable state requires it.
    - **Confirmed sub-task breakdown** (single isolated PR — no other layer has any change):
      - [x] **27.2.1.1** Data Gateway — N/A, no schema change.
      - [x] **27.2.2.1** Domain Service — try/catch wrapper + `isClientProfileUniqueConflict` P2002 helper (mirrors `updateClientProfile.ts`'s `isInstagramHandleConflict`) + `SET_UP_CLIENT_PROFILE_UNEXPECTED_ERROR_MESSAGE` constant in `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount.ts`; extend `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount.test.ts` with: generic-Error rejection → generic result not thrown; P2002 rejection → same generic result (proving the P2002 split is log-only); a `console.error` spy asserting both cases log.
      - [x] **27.2.3.1–27.2.6.1** Controller/UI/Hook/View — N/A. Fixing the service boundary neutralizes `useSetUpClientProfile.ts`'s stuck-spinner gap by construction; the hook itself is untouched.
  - **27.3: Email verification before session issuance** — `signupClient` grants a session immediately on account creation with no proof of email ownership. There is no `signupArtist` (artist accounts are manually provisioned per CLAUDE.md 5.1), so this is the only account-creation-time session issuance in the codebase.
    - **Design (confirmed):** Provider is Resend (new dependency + `src/lib/resend.ts` singleton wrapper mirroring `src/lib/stripe.ts`); no backfill needed (no real users to grandfather as verified). Verification UX is a 6-digit numeric code (not a magic link — resilient to email-client link prefetching) entered on a dedicated `/client/verify-email` page. Session-issuance model is "no session until verified": `signupClient` creates the `Account`, generates+stores a hashed code, sends the email, and returns a pending-verification result with no session fields — it no longer calls `createSession`. `verifyEmailCode` is the only path that issues the session for a fresh signup (auto-login on correct code, no separate password re-entry). `loginClient` gets defense-in-depth: since password ownership is already proven before this check, an unverified account with a correct password returns a distinct `pendingVerification` result (no session) rather than succeeding — this is not a new enumeration vector, unlike a pre-auth check would be. `resendVerificationCode` always returns the same generic result regardless of account existence/verified state/cooldown, for the same enumeration-safety reason `INVALID_CREDENTIALS_ERROR_MESSAGE` is generic. Brute-force protection: `MAX_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_ATTEMPTS = 5` wrong guesses invalidates the current code (forces a resend) since a 6-digit keyspace isn't safe against unlimited guessing; `EMAIL_VERIFICATION_CODE_EXPIRY_MS = 15 min`; `EMAIL_VERIFICATION_RESEND_COOLDOWN_MS = 60s` to throttle resend-spam/cost. Code storage is sha256 (`node:crypto createHash`, compared with `timingSafeEqual`) rather than scrypt — the code is short-lived and rate-limited, unlike a password, so scrypt's deliberate slowness has no benefit and would slow the verify path for nothing. The Resend call itself follows architecture.md §6 exactly (isolated try/catch, never rethrow, generic error on failure), mirroring `createConnectOnboardingLink.ts`. Playwright can't receive real emails, so `sendVerificationEmail` gets a test-only branch (env-flag gated, never set in production) that writes `{email, code}` to a capture sink instead of calling Resend; e2e reads the real code back through that sink, exercising the hashing/storage/verification logic unmodified. Implementation reminders: Prisma Update Atomicity in `verifyEmailCode`, Cooldown Logic in `resendVerificationCode` and Client-Side Form Usability in `VerifyEmailCodeForm`.
    - **Confirmed 6-layer sub-task breakdown** (each leaf = one isolated PR; do not combine):
      - [x] **27.3.1.1** Data Gateway — add `Account.emailVerifiedAt DateTime?`, `Account.emailVerificationCodeHash String?`, `Account.emailVerificationCodeExpiresAt DateTime?`, `Account.emailVerificationCodeSentAt DateTime?`, `Account.emailVerificationAttempts Int @default(0)` + migration. No app code, no backfill.
      - [x] **27.3.2.1** Domain Service — add `resend` npm dependency; `src/lib/resend.ts` singleton wrapper; add `RESEND_API_KEY`/`EMAIL_FROM` dummy env values to the `test` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
      - [x] **27.3.2.2** Domain Service — `services/generateEmailVerificationCode.ts` (pure helper: `crypto.randomInt` 6-digit code, sha256 hash, expiry timestamp; unit test).
      - [x] **27.3.2.3** Domain Service — `services/sendVerificationEmail.ts` (try/catch-wrapped `resend.emails.send`, per architecture.md §6; test-mode capture-sink branch for e2e; unit test with mocked `@/lib/resend`).
      - [x] **27.3.2.4** Domain Service — modify `signupClient.ts`: generate+persist code, call `sendVerificationEmail`, remove `createSession`, return the new pending-verification result shape; extend `signupClient.test.ts`.
      - [x] **27.3.2.5** Domain Service — `services/verifyEmailCode.ts` (hash/expiry/attempt-count validation, `timingSafeEqual`, code invalidation after max attempts, `createSession` on success; unit tests: correct/wrong/expired/max-attempts/already-verified/unknown-email).
      - [x] **27.3.2.6** Domain Service — `services/resendVerificationCode.ts` (cooldown-gated regenerate+resend, generic result regardless of account state; unit test).
      - [x] **27.3.2.7** Domain Service — modify `loginClient.ts`: unverified account + correct password short-circuits into `pendingVerification` (no session); extend `loginClient.test.ts`.
      - [x] **27.3.2.8** Domain Service — close the pre-verification squatting → account-takeover path (found during 27.3.2.7 review): today an attacker can sign up with a victim's booked email + the attacker's own password; the victim later enters the code (via the public verify page + resend) and `verifyEmailCode` verifies the account and issues a session with no password check, leaving a verified account whose password the attacker knows (no password-reset flow exists to recover). Fix: (1) `verifyEmailCode` input becomes `{ email, code, password }` and runs `verifyPassword` before reserving an attempt, so verification proves both inbox control *and* password knowledge (same generic error on password mismatch); (2) `signupClient` against an existing *unverified* account replaces `passwordHash` and issues a fresh code (old code invalidated) instead of `ACCOUNT_ALREADY_EXISTS`, so the real owner can always reclaim — an attacker re-squatting only causes ping-pong, never takeover. Tests: squatted account + victim's code without the attacker's password → rejected; victim re-signup → password replaced and old code dead; verified account re-signup still rejected. Sequenced before 27.3.3.1 so the action/schema layer is built on the final verify contract.
      - [x] **27.3.3.1** Controller/Action — `verifyEmailCodeInputSchema`/`resendVerificationCodeInputSchema` in `auth.schema.ts` (verify schema includes `password`, per 27.3.2.8); `verifyEmailCodeAction`/`resendVerificationCodeAction` in `actions.ts` (sets session cookie via existing `setSessionCookie` helper on successful verification).
      - [x] **27.3.3.2** Controller/Action — update `signupClientAction`/`loginClientAction` result types/branches to carry the pending-verification outcome through.
      - [x] **27.3.4.1** UI Primitive — `VerifyEmailCodeForm` component (6-digit input, resend button with cooldown countdown, error state; mirrors `ClientLoginForm`/`ClientSignupForm`, semantic tokens only).
      - [x] **27.3.4.2** UI Primitive — add a password field + `password`/`onPasswordChange` props to `VerifyEmailCodeForm`/`VerifyEmailCodeFormProps` (found during 27.3.5.1: `verifyEmailCodeAction` requires `password` per 27.3.2.8, but the 27.3.4.1 form has no such field).
      - [x] **27.3.5.1** Domain Hook — `useVerifyEmailCode.ts` (form state incl. `password` + resend cooldown timer + redirect to `/client` on success; hook test via `renderHook`, mirrors `useSwitchActiveRole.test.ts`).
      - [x] **27.3.5.2** Domain Hook — modify `useClientSignup.ts`/`useClientLogin.ts` to redirect to `/client/verify-email?email=...` on the pending-verification outcome; update/extend their hook tests.
      - [x] **27.3.6.1** View & Route — new `/client/verify-email` page; add its path to `PUBLIC_CLIENT_PATHS` in `src/proxy.ts`; `e2e/verify-email.spec.ts` with a `toHaveScreenshot()` assertion using the capture-sink bypass; update the existing client-signup e2e spec to route through verification.
  - **27.4: Session TTL/cleanup** — session rows are created on every login/signup and never pruned; `switchActiveRole`/`getSessionWithAccount` only filter expired rows at read time — no sweep/cron job exists. Growth/scale risk, not an active exploit: an ever-growing, unindexed `Session` table directly degrades the hot path of every authenticated request (`src/proxy.ts` hits Postgres on every matched request), not just an offline job's runtime.
    - **Design (confirmed):** No cron/scheduler infra exists anywhere in the repo today (no `vercel.json`, no `/api/cron` routes, no scheduled GitHub Actions, no cron/queue dependency), and the hosting platform is never confirmed in-repo. Trigger mechanism (user-confirmed): a new `.github/workflows/session-cleanup.yml` scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (daily `schedule:` cron `0 3 * * *` + `workflow_dispatch` for manual runs) — platform-agnostic rather than assuming Vercel Cron, and this repo already uses GitHub Actions for CI. The workflow does an authenticated `curl POST` (using `CRON_SECRET`/`APP_URL` repo secrets) to a new `src/app/api/cron/session-cleanup/route.ts` route, which mirrors the existing `src/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts` pattern (closest existing precedent for an externally-triggered, secret-verified endpoint). The route validates `Authorization: Bearer <CRON_SECRET>` via a length-safe `crypto.timingSafeEqual` compare (reject immediately on length mismatch before comparing, never throw; no DB touch at all on a bad/missing secret — mirrors the constant-time discipline already established for email verification codes in 27.3), returning `401` on failure. On a valid secret it delegates to the domain service inside a try/catch (architecture.md §6 discipline), returning generic `500` + server-side log (no PII) on failure or `200` with `{ deletedCount, durationMs }` on success for ops visibility in the Action's job log. Prisma's `deleteMany` has no `LIMIT`, so a single invocation against a large table risks a long-running transaction/lock; the domain service instead loops a raw-SQL batched delete (`DELETE FROM "Session" WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM "Session" WHERE "expiresAt" < now() LIMIT $1)` via `prisma.$executeRaw`), stopping when a batch returns 0 rows or a max-batch cap is hit, so one invocation's runtime is bounded regardless of backlog size. New constants `SESSION_CLEANUP_BATCH_SIZE = 1000` / `SESSION_CLEANUP_MAX_BATCHES = 20` (bounds one run to 20,000 deletions; a larger backlog just finishes on the next day's run). Concurrency safety is deliberate-no-locking: a raw `DELETE ... WHERE expiresAt < now()` is naturally idempotent, so an overlapping manual + scheduled run just has the later one delete 0 rows for already-removed ids — no read-then-write race exists. `Session.expiresAt` has no index today, so a `@@index([expiresAt])` migration is required or the batched delete's inner `SELECT` is a full table scan. `CRON_SECRET` is added to `.env.example` and the CI `test` job's dummy-env block (same non-secret-placeholder pattern as `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`/`UPLOADTHING_TOKEN`, and already planned for `RESEND_API_KEY` in 27.3.2.1) purely so the route module doesn't crash import-time env checks in CI — the workflow itself only ever runs against a real deployed `APP_URL`, never inside `ci.yml`'s Postgres-container job. Explicitly deferred, not bundled in: `getSessionWithAccount.ts` and `switchActiveRole.ts` independently hand-roll the same `expiresAt.getTime() <= Date.now()` check — a legitimate architecture.md §5 "Shared Logic Extraction" candidate, but orthogonal to pruning rows and out of this atomic scope.
    - **Confirmed 6-layer sub-task breakdown** (each leaf = one isolated PR; do not combine):
      - [x] **27.4.1.1** Data Gateway — add `@@index([expiresAt])` to the `Session` model + migration. No app code.
      - [x] **27.4.2.1** Domain Service — add `SESSION_CLEANUP_BATCH_SIZE` / `SESSION_CLEANUP_MAX_BATCHES` constants to `src/domains/auth/constants.ts`.
      - [x] **27.4.2.2** Domain Service — `services/pruneExpiredSessions.ts` (batched raw-SQL delete loop via `prisma.$executeRaw`, returns total deleted count; mocked-Prisma unit tests mirroring `switchActiveRole.test.ts`'s style: single partial batch, multi-batch loop terminating on a zero-row batch, loop terminating at `SESSION_CLEANUP_MAX_BATCHES`, and a zero-expired-rows no-op).
      - [x] **27.4.3.1** Controller/Action — `src/app/api/cron/session-cleanup/route.ts` `POST` handler (length-safe `timingSafeEqual` bearer-token check against `CRON_SECRET`, delegates to `pruneExpiredSessions`, try/catch → generic `500` + server-side log, `200` with `{ deletedCount, durationMs }` on success); add `CRON_SECRET` to `.env.example` and the CI dummy-env block; route-handler unit test invoking the exported `POST` directly with mocked service (missing secret → 401, mismatched secret → 401, success → 200 with mocked count, service throws → 500).
      - [x] **27.4.4.1** UI Primitive — N/A. No user-facing surface exists for a backend sweep job; reserved explicitly per the vertical-slice requirement rather than silently skipped.
      - [x] **27.4.5.1** Domain Hook — N/A. No client-side state to orchestrate.
      - [x] **27.4.6.1** View & Route — new `.github/workflows/session-cleanup.yml` (`schedule:` daily cron + `workflow_dispatch`, authenticated `curl POST` to the route using the `CRON_SECRET`/`APP_URL` repo secrets). This is the layer that actually wires the endpoint into a live, recurring invocation path — the closest analog this backend-only feature has to "View & Route."
  - **27.5: Audit trail on security-relevant events** — role switches, failed logins, and Set Up Client Profile links aren't logged anywhere; given CLAUDE.md's cancellation/precharge flagging requirements on `ClientProfile`, an audit trail on identity/role changes belongs at this level. Lowest urgency of the five: compliance/forensics value, not a live gap.
    - **Design (confirmed):** new append-only `AuditEvent` Prisma model — `eventType`/`outcome`/`reasonCode` are all DB-enforced enums (`AuditEventType`, `AuditEventOutcome`, `AuditReasonCode`), never free-form strings, so no typo'd value can ever land in the table. `accountId` is nullable with `onDelete: SetNull` (unlike `Session`'s `Cascade`) — an audit row must outlive account deletion for forensic value. `attemptedEmail` is populated only when there's no `accountId` to attach to (account-not-found/role-mismatch login failures), to detect enumeration/credential-stuffing scanning; this never leaves the server (the caller still gets the same generic error), so it's an accepted data-minimization tradeoff, same posture as 27.1's accepted timing side-channel. No IP-address field — no request-IP infra exists in the repo (same finding as 27.1). Indexed on `(accountId, createdAt)` and `(eventType, createdAt)` for compliance queries. Scoped to today's actual code, not 27.1–27.4's still-unimplemented designs, since phases have no guaranteed merge order. Single write choke point: `services/recordAuditEvent.ts` wraps `prisma.auditEvent.create` in its own try/catch (architecture.md §6 discipline) — never throws, always resolves `void`, logs `console.error` with only `eventType`/`reasonCode`/`accountId` on failure (never `attemptedEmail`), mirroring the ID-only logging convention in `billing/services/createArtistConnectAccount.ts`/`refundDeposit.ts`. Every call site awaits it (so a serverless function doesn't terminate before the write lands) but its result never affects the caller's return value or control flow. Call sites: `loginArtist.ts`/`loginClient.ts` audit **failures only** (`ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND`/`ROLE_MISMATCH` with `attemptedEmail`, `INVALID_PASSWORD` with `accountId`) — successful logins aren't in scope. `switchActiveRole.ts` audits both "not linked to X" rejections and the success path (all with `accountId`+`targetRole`); the session-not-found/expired branch is skipped (no reliable identity to attach). `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount.ts` (the Set Up Client Profile flow) calls `recordAuditEvent` once, after `prisma.$transaction(...)` resolves (decoupled from transaction rollback semantics), branching on the already-discriminated result — both rejection reasons and both success reasons (profile created vs. matched-existing), always with `accountId`. No presentation layer: no admin UI, query surface, retention/export policy, or IP capture — mirrors 27.4.4.1's precedent of explicitly reserving UI/Hook/View/Controller leaves as N/A for a backend-only, compliance-facing feature. Explicitly deferred: an audit-log viewer, retention/archival policy, auditing additional event types (successful logins, logout, 27.1's lockout triggers, 27.3's email-verification events), and out-of-band lockout notification emails to the account holder (raised during 27.1.2.3 review as a defense-in-depth addition to silent lockout — has its own external-side-effect/delivery-reliability concerns per architecture.md §6, orthogonal to this phase's append-only DB log) — bundling those here would violate the atomic-scope rule.

### 📦 Phase 28: Domain Testing Architecture & Test Layer Migration
- **Status:** 28.1–28.3 scoped; 28.4–28.5 remain unscoped (each will get its own layered breakdown pass closer to when it's picked up). 28.1 is sequenced *ahead of* Phase 27's remaining work (see Phase 27 Sequencing note).
- **Objectives:** Migrate all existing domain tests to use a lightweight, mocked Prisma layer for fast unit testing, while establishing a dedicated real-database integration and E2E testing framework to validate complex multi-domain database constraints and transaction boundary guarantees. Extended scope, priority-ordered: (1) controller/action-layer (`actions.ts`) test coverage — the thin action layer doing session-check + validation + redirect branching is currently untested despite testing.md's edge-case mandate, and it directly wraps the security-sensitive paths in Phase 27 above; (2) hook-level unit tests using `@testing-library/react`'s `renderHook` for every domain hook.
- **Current-state findings (drives the breakdown below):**
  - No Prisma mock exists anywhere (no `__mocks__`, no `vitest-mock-extended`). All 67 `src/domains/**/*.test.ts` files import the real `prisma` singleton from `@/lib/prisma` and run `beforeEach`/`afterEach` create/delete cycles against live Postgres; CI's `test` job only passes because it runs `prisma migrate deploy` first. These are integration tests in unit-test clothing.
  - `architecture.md` §7 ("No Live DB Queries in Unit Tests… MUST completely mock the Prisma client") and `testing.md` §1 ("Database Cleansing Invariant": real-DB `beforeEach` wipe) contradict each other; the codebase follows `testing.md`, violating `architecture.md`.
  - E2E is already mature: 26 `e2e/*.spec.ts` specs against real Postgres via raw-`pg` `global-setup.ts`/`global-teardown.ts`/`dbHelpers.ts`, with a dedicated CI job. The E2E half of the objective is met; the missing tier is **non-browser real-DB integration tests**.
  - `actions.ts` exists in 4 domains (auth, billing, booking, scheduling — 1,077 lines combined); only `auth/actions.test.ts` exists (covers 4 of 9 auth actions); billing, booking and scheduling have none. `directory` has no actions.
  - 21 hooks exist; only 2 are tested (`useSwitchActiveRole.test.ts`, `useSetUpClientProfile.test.ts` — `// @vitest-environment jsdom` + `renderHook` + `vi.mock("@/domains/auth/actions")`), which become the convention for 28.5.
  - No domain has a `queries/` folder yet (reads live under `services/`); out of scope here — Phase 28 does not restructure source folders.

- [x] **28.1: Mocked-Prisma Foundation & Rules Reconciliation**
  - **Design (confirmed):** Mock library is `vitest-mock-extended` (`mockDeep<PrismaClient>()`, typed against `@/generated/prisma/client` — the adapter-based generated client `src/lib/prisma.ts` instantiates), chosen over hand-rolled `vi.fn()` stubs so the mock surface can never drift from the real client's types and no test author has to remember to stub every delegate method. The helper lives at `src/testUtils/prismaMock.ts` and is **opt-in per test file**: importing it registers `vi.mock("@/lib/prisma", () => ({ prisma: prismaMock }))` plus `beforeEach(() => mockReset(prismaMock))`. It is deliberately **not** wired globally in `vitest.setup.ts` — a global mock would silently break the 4 existing `*.stripe-integration.test.ts` files and the future 28.3 integration tier, both of which require the real client, and would let un-migrated real-DB tests "pass" against empty mocks during the 28.2 rollout. The helper also installs a default `prismaMock.$transaction` implementation that invokes interactive-transaction callbacks with `prismaMock` itself (and resolves array-form batches), re-applied after every `mockReset`, so services such as `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount` (callback-form `$transaction`) are unit-testable without per-file boilerplate; individual tests may still override it to simulate a rejected transaction (the exact scenario 27.2's P2002 handling needs). Rules reconciliation: `architecture.md` §7's mocking mandate is scoped explicitly to domain unit tests (`src/domains/**/*.test.ts`, excluding `*.integration.test.ts` / `*.stripe-integration.test.ts`); `testing.md` §1's "Database Cleansing Invariant" is re-scoped to the `*.integration.test.ts` tier introduced in 28.3 (the only tier permitted to write to a DB besides E2E and Stripe integration). Explicitly deferred: the `testing.md` §4 step-order mismatch vs. `ci.yml` (`prisma generate` runs before `migrate deploy` in CI, the reverse of what §4 prescribes) — real but orthogonal, would violate atomic scope here.

Behaviour-preserving: every existing `it(...)` case keeps an equivalent mocked case (no case silently dropped); any case whose *only* value was a real DB behaviour (unique-constraint violation, cascade delete, transaction rollback, `@default`/`@updatedAt` population) is **not** faked with a hand-thrown error — it is listed in that PR's description as a 28.3 integration-tier candidate instead, so coverage moves tiers rather than disappearing. Time-dependent services are pinned with `vi.useFakeTimers()`/`vi.setSystemTime()` rather than relying on wall-clock fixture dates.   - **Design (confirmed):** New `*.integration.test.ts` convention (mirrors `*.stripe-integration.test.ts`) with its own `vitest.integration.config.mts` + `test:integration` script + CI job against a `postgres:16` service container, excluded from the main `vitest.config.mts`. Targets only what mocks structurally cannot prove: unique-constraint races (the `ClientProfile` `instagramHandle`/`email` TOCTOU P2002 race 27.2 documents), double-booking / adjacent-slot overflow capping (CLAUDE.md invariant #1) under concurrent writes, `onDelete` cascade/SetNull behaviour, `$transaction` rollback guarantees, plus every candidate handed off by 28.2's migrated tests (see Sequencing note). Fixture isolation: unique-per-test data (`randomUUID`-suffixed handles/emails, `@example.com`) plus a `beforeEach` wipe bounded to tracked ids via `src/testUtils/integrationDb.ts` (not truncate — it races a shared/dev DB; not per-test rollback — it cannot prove commit-time behaviour such as P2002 under concurrent transactions or `$transaction` rollback). Satisfies testing.md §1's Database Cleansing Invariant. Parallelism: `fileParallelism: false` (single shared DB); concurrency is exercised *within* a test via `Promise.allSettled`, asserting outcome invariants (exactly one winner), never ordering. Fixtures: tests own their data through the real `@/lib/prisma` (no `vi.mock`); they do not reuse `e2e/global-setup.ts` (raw-`pg`, E2E-specific `.fixture.json`). Safety guard: the integration setup refuses to run unless `DATABASE_URL` targets localhost/a `*test*` database, so the wipe can never touch a real DB. CI: dedicated `integration-tests` job (no Stripe secrets, so it also runs on fork PRs). Sequencing: 28.2.2.5 has landed, so 28.3.2.5 is unblocked. - [ ] **28.7: Missing Session/Ownership Guards on Controller Actions**
  - **Design (confirmed):** Surfaced by the 28.4 survey: booking's `approveBookingRequest` (no callers, legacy), `declineBookingRequest`, `reviewBookingRequestAction` and `confirmProposedBookingAction` have no session/ownership guard, and every scheduling action takes `artistId` from the client payload with no session guard (validation.md §2). `confirmTimeSlotAction` has no callers but is an exported `"use server"` function, i.e. an unauthenticated slot-write endpoint for any `artistId`; scheduling cannot verify `bookingRequestId` ownership without reading booking tables (architecture.md §1) or importing booking (§4), so it is deleted rather than guarded (`reviewBookingRequestAction` supersedes it; the service-layer `confirmTimeSlot.ts` stays because booking reuses `createBookedTimeSlots`/`isSlotConflict`). `getAvailableSlotsAction` stays intentionally public (the guest booking wizard calls it). Guards live in the controller, matching `rescheduleApprovedBookingAction` and billing: `requireArtistId()` (checks `activeRole`, not `role`) then `requireOwnedRequest()`; a non-artist returns the "signed in as an artist" message, a non-owner/missing request returns `REQUEST_NOT_FOUND_ERROR_MESSAGE` (no enumeration). Ownership is immutable (`BookingRequest.artistId` never changes), so check-then-act cannot race. Scheduling settings actions drop `artistId` from their Zod schemas and derive it from the session; the hooks keep sending a now-ignored `artistId` (Zod strips unknown keys), so no UI/Hook/View change is needed. Each guard leaf creates the domain's `actions.test.ts` with a guard table (signed-out, `activeRole: "CLIENT"`, non-owner, owner; service NOT called on any rejection; hostile `artistId` payload ignored); 28.4.3.4 / 28.4.3.6–28.4.3.8 extend those files and assert guarded behaviour. **Flagged, not fixed:** (1) `approveBookingRequest` is guarded here but should be deleted in a separate follow-up; (2) `setBookingRequestStatus` has no status precondition (declining an already-APPROVED request orphans its BOOKED slots and skips strike logic); (3) the now-ignored `artistId` prop/payload key in `useWeeklyHoursSettings`/`useScheduleOverrides`/`WeeklyHoursSettings`/`BlackoutDateSettings` is dead and should be cleaned up separately; (4) `requireArtistId` is now duplicated in billing, booking and scheduling (architecture.md §4.B shared-logic extraction candidate).

### 📦 Phase 54: Private Portal, `/@handle` Artist Profiles & Passwordless Client Booking ◄ CURRENT FOCUS
> Pivots the front door to a single domain (vettr.studio): artists share `vettr.studio/@handle` (public profile + booking intake in client view), `/` becomes a Private Portal Gate (no public marketplace directory), and clients authenticate with a 6-digit email code instead of a password — inline at the final "Submit request" step of a booking, or from the portal gate. Signed-in users are routed by `Session.activeRole` (existing Artist/Client view switcher). **Sequenced after 27.8** (takeover hotfix).
- **Design (confirmed):**
  - **Decisions:** email code now, SMS later (Phase 55 stub); magic links rejected (27.3's prefetch finding + they lose the in-tab draft). Clients become fully passwordless, artists keep passwords, `Account.passwordHash` becomes nullable (no real users, no backfill). New `Artist.handle` column (lowercase, unique, backfilled from `lower(instagramHandle)`). Profile content is *derived* from existing data (service menu = the 4 `ComplexityTier`s with `ArtistDepositSetting` deposits + `TIER_BASELINE_BUDGETS`; portfolio = `TierReferenceImage`; policies = deposit, `CANCELLATION_WINDOW_HOURS`, strike → precharge) — editable versions stay in Phases 34/35/39.
  - **Routing:** `next.config.ts` `rewrites()` maps `/@:handle` → `/at/:handle` and `/@:handle/book` → `/at/:handle/book` (a literal `@handle` folder would be a parallel-route slot). Verified against the bundled Next 16 docs: `@` needs no escaping; the param arrives decoded; `?service=` survives; the proxy sees the original path (so `/@x` stays public with no DB hit — matcher is `/artist`/`/client` only); Server Actions post to the browser URL and are rewritten the same way — the 54.1.6.x e2e tests prove each. `/@handle` is canonical (`alternates.canonical`, root `metadataBase` from `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` with the localhost fallback used in `createConnectOnboardingLink.ts`); uppercase handle → 308 to lowercase; unknown → `notFound()` with a themed `src/app/not-found.tsx` and no `loading.tsx`/Suspense above the lookup (keeps the 404 status). `/book/[artistId]` → `permanentRedirect` to `/@handle/book`; `/artists` is deleted and left to the themed 404 (no redirect: pre-launch nothing links to it, and a 308 is cached forever).
  - **Handle migration:** created with `--create-only` and hand-edited (precedents `20260923231158`, `20260925202250`): add nullable → backfill `lower(regexp_replace(btrim("instagramHandle"),'^@',''))` → `DO $$` guard raising on duplicates/reserved words/regex failures → `SET NOT NULL` → unique index `Artist_handle_key` → CHECKs (lowercase, regex). `src/lib/artistHandle.ts` owns the normaliser, `ARTIST_HANDLE_REGEX`, `RESERVED_ARTIST_HANDLES` (incl. blocking a `.rsc` suffix) and `artistHandleSchema`. Hand-provisioned artists must now set `handle` (add to the 53.1.6.1 runbook).
  - **Profile page:** the `directory` domain is repurposed as the public artist read model (narrow DTO, no email/Stripe fields). The page composes `getPublicArtistProfileByHandle` + `getArtistDepositSettings` + `getTierReferenceImages` via `Promise.all` in try/catch (architecture.md §3: read-only, presentational); service-menu assembly lives in a pure `booking/lib/buildServiceMenu.ts`.
  - **Email OTP (auth-owned):** new `EmailOtpChallenge` table — one row per normalised email, `purpose` (`CLIENT_SIGN_IN` | `BOOKING_SUBMISSION`), `codeHash`, `expiresAt`, `attempts`, `sentAt`, `consumedAt`, rolling send window (`windowStartedAt`, `windowSendCount`); no FK (booking codes exist before any Account). Reuses `generateEmailVerificationCode`/`hashEmailVerificationCode`/`sendVerificationEmail` + the e2e capture sink and the 15-min expiry / 5-attempt / 60s-cooldown constants; adds a 10-sends-per-24h-per-address cap (an hourly cap would still allow ~600 guesses/day), and for sign-in a 1.5s response floor with a 1s send timeout. Every guard is an atomic conditional `updateMany` mirroring `verifyEmailCode`/`resendVerificationCode`/`recordFailedLoginAttempt`; an attempt is reserved before comparing (`timingSafeEqual`); the code is consumed by a guarded `updateMany` inside the caller's transaction. Portal sign-in sends *only* to an Account with role CLIENT + `clientProfileId` and returns an identical response otherwise (27.7's confirmed direction; no email-bombing vector); an ARTIST-home account is never issued an OTP session (email access + role switcher must not bypass the artist password). Booking codes are always sent, after full server prevalidation (schema + `validateComplexity`).
  - **Booking verification outcomes:** CLIENT account with profile → CLIENT session, booking attaches, blank fields only; ARTIST-home account (artist-only or dual-role) → no session, post-proof message ("sign in as artist → switch to client view" / "set up client profile first"); no account + unlinked profile with that email → create Account(CLIENT, null password, `emailVerifiedAt` now) and link, blank fields only; no account + profile linked elsewhere → reject; no account/profile + IG handle free → create both; handle taken → reject, rollback keeps the code valid. `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount` is deliberately **not** reused (its handle-first matching would let a verified user claim someone else's unlinked guest profile).
  - **Verify + submit orchestration:** application service `booking/services/submitBookingRequestWithEmailOtp.ts` (booking → auth is the allowed direction): `validateComplexity` → auth `verifyEmailOtpAndProvisionClient` (one transaction: consume + provision + session; `createSession` gains an optional `tx`) → booking `createBookingRequest` (the write shared with the signed-in path). Failure split: if the booking create fails after verification, the session is already committed and the cookie set — the client retries via the signed-in path with no second code. `setSessionCookie` moves to a non-`"use server"` `auth/sessionCookie.ts`. The unverified guest path (`resolveGuestClientProfile`, whose by-handle branch overwrites a profile's email/phone/name/DOB) is removed in 54.6.
  - **Wizard:** new order Service → Intake (uploads/tags/notes/budget/payment method) → Date & Slot → Details & Verify (IG handle, name, DOB, email, phone, then the inline code). A signed-in CLIENT session skips the code; an ARTIST session is treated as a guest; `?service=` preselects the tier and starts at Intake; the empty-string optional-phone bug is fixed in the new schema. The new wizard is built alongside the old one and a single View leaf (54.5.6.1) switches over.
  - **Portal gate:** signed-in visitors redirect by `activeRole` (fixes `src/app/page.tsx` checking `session.role`); signed-out visitors see Find your artist (→ `/@handle`), inline client sign-in by code, and the artist sign-in link. The client portal's "Find an artist" link becomes an inline finder.
  - **E2E:** seeded CLIENT sessions + cookie-injection `loginAsClient` (54.2) land before `/client/login` turns OTP; only `client-auth.spec` drives the real OTP screen (code read from the capture sink). Every new page asserts `toHaveScreenshot()` with linux + win32 baselines.
  - **Supersedes/overlaps (noted here only — those items' text and checkboxes are the user's to update):** 27.3 client parts retired by 54.8 (helpers reused); 27.7 implemented by 54.3.2.6; 28.4.3.5 replaced by 54.5.3.3/54.5.3.4/54.6.3.1 (guest-path cases dropped); 28.6 superseded (both services deleted; P2002 concern moves to 54.5.2.2/54.5.2.6); 28.7 still needed (mark `getAvailableSlotsAction` intentionally public); 30.1 partly covered by 54.5.4.4 (confirmation email still open); 38.1 moot; Phase 52 becomes artist-only; 53.1.6.1/53.3.1.1 gain `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://vettr.studio`, the handle requirement and apex/www handling; 39.1 should add handle editing using `artistHandleSchema`.
  - **Flagged, not fixed (out of atomic scope):** `useArtistLogin` follows an unvalidated `redirectTo` (the new client hook validates from day one); no server-side slot-availability re-check at submit; the UploadThing endpoint has no auth; `designReferenceImageUrls` accept any host; `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount`'s handle-first match can claim unlinked profiles; a lost-response retry on the signed-in submit path can duplicate a booking (no idempotency key). **Also, until 54.6 lands:** `resolveGuestClientProfile`'s by-handle branch lets anyone who knows a client's public Instagram handle replace that profile's email; `signupClient` then finds the profile by the new email, links a new account to it and mails the code to the attacker, who ends up with a verified session over the victim's bookings. So 54.5–54.8 gate 53.3. The handle-first claim in `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount` is now 58.1.
  - **Rule exceptions (signed off with this breakdown):** (1) 54.6 and 54.8 run outer layers first (View/Controller before Domain/Data) since deleting a service before its caller won't compile; (2) Data leaves 54.1.1.1 and 54.8.1.1 also carry the fixture-only test edits their NOT NULL/CHECK changes force, so CI stays green; (3) prep leaf 54.3.2.3 (null-tolerant `verifyPassword`) lands early so 54.5.1.1's nullable `passwordHash` is a pure Data leaf; (4) scope addition 54.7 (verified email is the fixed client identity — otherwise a client could set their profile email to someone else's address and block that person's first booking).
  - **§7 edge cases:** *Concurrency* — double code request (cooldown inside the atomic update, row created with skip-duplicates); parallel guesses (attempt reserved before compare); double verify (guarded consume → one session, one booking); same new email/handle racing (unique constraints, P2002 → generic retry, rollback keeps the loser's code valid). *Failure* — verified but booking create fails (session kept, retry via the signed-in path); Resend down (never throws, generic "code sent", cooldown kept → no retry storm); DB error (generic retryable message, logs `{operation, reason, accountId?}` only). *Privacy* — sign-in enumeration (eligible-only sends, identical copy, 1.5s floor, send timeout below the floor); post-proof outcomes visible only to the inbox owner (handle probing capped at 5 per code). *Security* — brute force/email bombing (60s cooldown, 10 per 24h, 5 attempts; per-IP limits deferred to the Phase 52 prerequisite). *Invariants* — `expiresAt > now` on the Node clock; consumed/invalidated code nulled; null password → false; emails normalised in schema + service with a CHECK on the challenge table; draft edited after the code is sent → full server re-validation, UI resets on email change.

### 📦 Phase 56: Deposit Payment Integrity (pre-go-live)
> Found on 2026-10-07 by checking the deposit flow against the idempotency key → record-the-intent-first → webhook-timeline design. No real money moves until 53.3 (staging stays in Stripe test mode), so nothing here interrupts Phase 54, but every item gates 53.3. Every item is *unscoped* and needs its own 6-layer breakdown pass before any code. Phase 57 (`04-future-epics.md`) is the long-term version: an append-only payment event ledger and a fix for the booking ↔ billing dependency.
- **Design constraint (proposed):** new payment state (refund status, dispute records) goes into billing-owned tables keyed by `bookingRequestId`. It must not become new `BookingRequest` columns written through booking's narrow functions, so that Phase 57 builds on this work instead of migrating it.
- **Order:** numeric. 56.1 is a cheap spike that decides which refund events 56.6/56.7 listen for. 56.3 is the Data Gateway prerequisite for 56.4. 56.4 and 56.5 share a root cause (the fixed idempotency key): design them together, ship them as separate items.
- [ ] **56.1: Prove Which Stripe Events a Deposit Refund Emits** — *unscoped, spike.*
  - The webhook only handles `refund.updated` with status `succeeded`, but the comments in `refundDeposit.ts` and `confirmDepositRefund.ts` name `charge.refunded`.
  - A card refund that is created already `succeeded` may never emit `refund.updated`. If so, the refund backstop is dead code.
  - Nothing proves delivery today: `depositRefundLifecycle.stripe-integration.test.ts` calls `confirmDepositRefund` directly.
  - Use the Stripe CLI (`stripe listen`) in test mode to record which events fire for an immediate card refund, a pending refund and a failed refund. Subscribe the route to the right events and fix the stale comments.
  - This is the first proof of the refund backstop, so 53.3.1.2's live-money refund is no longer that first proof.
- [ ] **56.2: Deposit Paid on a Cancelled or Declined Booking** — *unscoped.*
  - `confirmDepositPayment` sets `depositPaid` without checking the booking's status.
  - Both cancel paths (`cancelBookingRequest`, `cancelApprovedBookingAsArtist`) only refund when `depositPaid` is already true.
  - So a webhook delayed by an outage (Stripe retries for days), or a payment made from a tab left open after cancelling, leaves a `CANCELLED_*` booking with `depositPaid = true`. Nobody refunds the money.
  - Declining an `APPROVED` booking has the same result (28.7 flagged-not-fixed item 2: `setBookingRequestStatus` has no status check).
  - Design pass: when a payment is confirmed on a non-`APPROVED` booking, record it and issue a full refund. Decide whether cancelling should also cancel an open PaymentIntent.
  - Concurrency: a cancel racing the webhook must produce exactly one refund. The per-booking refund idempotency key already dedupes at Stripe.
  - The new branches need unit tests, plus a real-DB race case in the integration tier.
- [ ] **56.3: Unique Stripe Identifiers on Deposit Records** — *unscoped, small.*
  - `stripePaymentIntentId` and `stripeRefundId` have no unique constraint, so `getBookingRequestByPaymentIntentId` uses `findFirst` and relies on "safe in practice".
  - Add unique indexes (no real users, so no backfill) and switch to `findUnique`.
  - This is the Data Gateway prerequisite for 56.4's lookups. If the design constraint above moves these ids into a billing-owned table, this becomes that table's Data Gateway leaf.
- [ ] **56.4: Stale PaymentIntent After the 24h Idempotency-Key Window** — *unscoped.*
  - The idempotency key is fixed per booking (`deposit-intent:<bookingRequestId>`), and Stripe only keeps keys for 24h. A visit after 24h creates a second PaymentIntent, and `recordDepositPaymentIntent` overwrites `stripePaymentIntentId`.
  - If the old PaymentIntent is then paid, `confirmDepositPayment` returns not-found. The webhook route ignores that result and answers 200, so Stripe stops retrying and the payment is never recorded. If both PaymentIntents are paid, the client is charged twice.
  - Design pass:
    - Reuse a stored PaymentIntent that is still open instead of creating a new one. Retrieve it, then update the amount, or cancel and recreate it, if the amount changed.
    - Resolve unknown PaymentIntents through the `metadata.bookingRequestId` already set at creation.
    - Treat not-found as a logged critical alert (53.7), not a silent 200.
- [ ] **56.5: Deposit Creation Lockout and Uncaught Stripe Errors** — *unscoped.*
  - Reusing the fixed key with different parameters makes Stripe reject the call with an idempotency error for up to 24h. The parameters change when the artist edits the tier deposit, when the client is flagged for precharge, or when the artist's Connect `chargesEnabled` flips `on_behalf_of`/`transfer_data`.
  - `stripe.paymentIntents.create` has no try/catch (architecture.md §6.1, §8.B). Nor do `createDepositPaymentIntentAction` or `useDepositPayment`, so the rejection escapes uncaught and the hook's `isLoading` never resets (a stuck spinner).
  - Fix:
    - Make the key vary with the parameters that can change, or reuse the PaymentIntent per 56.4.
    - Wrap the Stripe call and return a generic retryable error, logging ids only.
    - Reset the hook's state on rejection.
- [ ] **56.6: Refund Status Lifecycle (Pending / Failed)** — *unscoped.*
  - `refundDeposit` sets `depositRefunded = true` as soon as `refunds.create` returns, even when the refund is still `pending`. Nothing handles a refund that later fails, so the booking reads as refunded while the client never got the money.
  - Record a refund intent as `PENDING` before calling Stripe (architecture.md §6.2). Move it to `SUCCEEDED`/`FAILED` from the events 56.1 identifies. `depositRefunded` becomes a derived view of that status.
  - Status changes must follow Stripe's event time or a fixed precedence of states, not arrival order. Webhooks are at-least-once and unordered, and this is the first deposit state that can move backwards.
  - Prerequisite for 56.7.
- [ ] **56.7: Retry Refunds Whose Stripe Call Failed** — *unscoped.*
  - If `stripe.refunds.create` itself fails, no refund exists on Stripe, so no webhook will ever arrive.
  - Both cancel paths only `console.error`. `cancelBookingRequest`'s comment, which says the webhook backstop reconciles this, is wrong for this case.
  - Add a bounded, idempotent retry for refund intents (from 56.6) that are still `PENDING` with no Stripe refund id. The 27.4 session-cleanup cron route and workflow are the precedent.
  - Reuse the per-booking refund idempotency key, so a retry after a lost response can't refund twice.
  - Raise a critical alert after N failed attempts (53.7).
- [ ] **56.8: Disputes and Failed Payments** — *unscoped.*
  - The webhook ignores `charge.dispute.*` events entirely. A chargeback on a deposit would go unnoticed: Stripe debits the platform for disputes on destination charges, and evidence has a deadline.
  - `payment_intent.payment_failed` is only logged.
  - Minimum for go-live: record dispute events against the booking and raise a critical alert (53.7).
  - Artist-facing dispute UI and evidence submission are out of scope. Decide whether an open dispute blocks further deposit actions on that booking.
- [ ] **56.9: Out-of-Order `account.updated` Events** — *unscoped, small.*
  - `syncArtistConnectAccountStatus` writes whichever event arrives last, but Stripe doesn't guarantee delivery order. A delayed older event can overwrite fresh `chargesEnabled`/`payoutsEnabled` values.
  - A stale `true` makes `createDepositPaymentIntent` send `on_behalf_of` to an account that can't take charges, so the deposit can't be created. A stale `false` sends the deposit to the platform instead of the artist.
  - Fix: retrieve the account from Stripe in the handler and write its current values, or skip events older than a stored `event.created`.
- [ ] **56.10: Cancel Allowlist on the Server** — *unscoped, small.*
  - `cancelBookingRequest` blocks only `CANCELLED_BY_CLIENT`, `DECLINED` and `COMPLETED` (`cancelBookingRequest.ts:14`). The UI uses an allowlist instead (`ClientBookingActions.tsx:45-49`), so `NO_SHOW` and `CANCELLED_BY_ARTIST` are blocked only in the browser.
  - A client who calls `cancelBookingRequestAction` directly on their own `NO_SHOW` booking rewrites it to `CANCELLED_BY_CLIENT`, erasing the no-show record, and `refundDeposit` (which has no status check) refunds the deposit that a no-show forfeits (CLAUDE.md 7.3).
  - `cancelBookingRequest.test.ts` has no case for either status.
  - Fix: allow only `PENDING`, `AWAITING_SLOT_CONFIRMATION` and `APPROVED`, from one constant in booking shared by the service and the UI so they can't drift. Add unit tests for `NO_SHOW` and `CANCELLED_BY_ARTIST`. Decide whether `refundDeposit`'s callers should also refuse a non-cancelled status.
  - Same family as 56.2 (handlers that don't check booking status): design them together, ship them separately.

### 📦 Phase 58: Identity & Authorization Hardening (pre-go-live)
> Found on 2026-10-07 by checking a list of 24 suspected architecture gaps against the code. Most were already built; these are the ones that held up. No real users yet, so nothing here interrupts Phase 54, but every item gates 53.3. Every item is *unscoped* and needs its own 6-layer breakdown pass before any code. The unverified guest-profile takeover is not an item here: 54.5–54.8 remove it, and they gate 53.3 (see the "Flagged, not fixed" line under Phase 54).
- **Order:** numeric, with 58.1 first (highest severity). 58.3 and 58.4 should wait for 28.8, 54.5 and 54.8, which rewrite much of the same code.
- [ ] **58.1: Guest-Profile Claim Guard** — *unscoped.*
  - `setUpClientProfileAction` only needs a session (`auth/actions.ts:129-155`). `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount` links a profile matched by Instagram handle even when that profile's email differs from the account's (`linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount.ts:81-121`, pinned by the test at `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount.test.ts:122-164`).
  - So any account, including an artist's, can claim an unlinked guest client's profile just by knowing their public handle. After switching to client view, that account can read and cancel the client's bookings with other artists.
  - The real client is locked out: signup hits the 27.8 silent guard (`signupClient.ts:46-55`) and OTP sign-in refuses them.
  - Fix: link only a profile whose email equals the account's own email; reject a handle match with a different email using the existing generic "already linked" error, so nothing is enumerable. Update the pinned test. Design pass: whether a handle match should instead require a code sent to the profile's email.
  - 54.6 shrinks the pool of unlinked profiles but does not remove this path.
- [ ] **58.2: Lowercase Client Instagram Handles** — *unscoped.*
  - `instagramHandleSchema` trims and strips `@` but never lowercases (`clientProfileValidation.ts:10-20`), and `ClientProfile_instagramHandle_key` is a plain unique index. `@MyHandle` and `@myhandle` become two profiles for one Instagram account.
  - A flagged client can reset `cancellationCount` and `enforcePrecharge` for free by re-booking in another case, which breaks CLAUDE.md core constraint 4.
  - Fix: lowercase in the shared schema (used by booking and auth) and add a lowercase CHECK on `ClientProfile.instagramHandle`, as `Artist_handle_lowercase_check` did in 54.1.1.1. The migration must guard on existing case-variant collisions the way `20261006182220_add_artist_handle` does. Pre-launch, so only fixtures need updating.
- [ ] **58.3: Normalise Email on Every Path** — *unscoped.*
  - Only the OTP paths use `normalizedEmailSchema`. Booking, login, signup, verify and resend use a raw `z.email()` (`booking.schema.ts:193`, `auth.schema.ts:12,20,47,54`), and the unique indexes on `Account.email` and `ClientProfile.email` are case-sensitive.
  - A client who signed up as `Me@X.com` is silently never sent a sign-in code (`requestClientSignInCode.ts:49-58` looks up the lowercase form and finds nothing). That becomes a lockout once 54.8 removes client passwords. It also allows case-variant duplicate profiles.
  - Overlap: 54.5.3.1 normalises the new booking schema, and 54.8 deletes signup and client login. What remains after those: artist login, lowercase CHECKs on both email columns (mirroring `EmailOtpChallenge_email_lowercase_check`), and any existing mixed-case rows.
  - Design-pass option (from the 54.5.2.1 review, 2026-10-08): a branded `NormalizedEmail` type returned by `normalizeEmail`/`normalizedEmailSchema` (`src/lib/email.ts`) and required by `issueEmailOtp`, `checkEmailOtpCode` and the verify/provision services, so an un-normalised string fails at compile time instead of relying on each service re-normalising (as `issueEmailOtp` does today). Scope it after 54.8, when the remaining email callers are known.
- [ ] **58.4: Thrown-Error Isolation and Stuck Forms** — *unscoped.*
  - The guest submit has no try/catch and no transaction (`booking/actions.ts:143-212`). It throws a raw P2002 on a concurrent first booking, and every time when an existing handle is submitted with another profile's email (`resolveGuestClientProfile.ts:25-35` then hits `email @unique`). `clientBudgetRangeSchema` has no maximum (`booking.schema.ts:112-120`), so an oversized budget overflows `Decimal(10,2)`.
  - `signupClient`, `loginClient`, `loginArtist` and `switchActiveRole` also let DB errors escape.
  - Their hooks set `isSubmitting` and never reset it when the action throws (`useVisualBookingForm.ts:182-196`, `useClientSignup.ts:26-45`, `useClientLogin.ts`, `useArtistLogin.ts`, `useSwitchActiveRole.ts`). The button stays stuck and shows no message (architecture.md §8.B).
  - Fix: typed failure results from the services (the pattern `linkOrCreateClientProfileForAccount` and `signInClientWithEmailOtp` already follow), `try/finally` in the hooks, and a budget maximum.
  - Overlap: 28.8, 54.5.2.3 and 54.8 replace most of the guest, signup and client-login code. Scope what is left (artist login, role switch, the hooks, the budget maximum) after those.
- [ ] **58.5: Page-Level Artist Session Guard** — *unscoped, small.*
  - `/artist/[artistId]` pages read data by the URL id without comparing it to the session (`artist/[artistId]/page.tsx:37-43`, and the requests, appointments, calendar and checkout pages). Only `proxy.ts` enforces it (`proxy.ts:54-61`). Server actions are already guarded, so this is defence in depth.
  - The bundled Next 16 docs say Proxy "should not be your only line of defense" (`node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/authentication.md:1121`) and warn that layout checks don't re-run on navigation (`:1352`).
  - Fix: a shared server helper (an ARTIST-active session whose `artistId` equals the URL id, otherwise `notFound()`) called by each page or its data read, not by the layout.
- [ ] **58.6: Identity Hardening** — *unscoped, small.* Three latent issues that can't be exploited today:
  - Action inputs are built as `{ artistId, ...parsed.data }` (`billing/actions.ts:86,130`, `scheduling/actions.ts:103,127,151`, `booking/actions.ts:344,367`), so a future schema field with the same name would override the session id. It is safe today only because Zod strips unknown keys. Put the session ids last.
  - `getCurrentSession` is exported from a `"use server"` file (`auth/actions.ts:329`), which makes it a server action that returns the raw session id. No client file imports it today. Move it to a server-only auth module, the same move 54.5.3.2 makes for `setSessionCookie`.
  - `switchActiveRole` checks `artistId` but not `Account.role` (`switchActiveRole.ts:25`). Artist access needing a password therefore depends on no CLIENT-home account ever getting an `artistId`. Check the role there, or add a DB CHECK tying `role` to `artistId`. Phase 59's client passkeys rely on the same invariant (a passkey session must never reach artist access through the role switcher), so 58.6 must land before 59.
